prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: ফসল মৌসুমভিত্তিক বপন, কর্তন ও ফলন সূচি (language bn).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ফসল" · longest unbreakable word 69px · one-line width 149px
  col 2: header "বপন" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 263px
  col 3: header "কাটা" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 239px
  col 4: header "ফলন (টন/হেক্টর)" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 108px
  col 5: header "মন্তব্য" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 1035px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A crop-by-crop season reference: compare when each crop is sown and harvested, what it yields, and any notes.","reading":"Primarily row-wise: fix the crop in col 1, read cols 2–3 as one sowing-to-harvest window, then col 4 yield and col 5 caveat; secondarily scan down the date columns to compare seasons.","groups":["col 1 is the row anchor","cols 2–3 are a paired timing unit and must stay adjacent","col 4 is the quantitative outcome","col 5 is free-text commentary attached to the whole row"],"keep_intact":["crop names in col 1","month/season names and date ranges in cols 2–3","yield numbers and the টন/হেক্টর unit in col 4","row identity"],"may_wrap":["date ranges at spaces and em dashes","the yield header between ফলন and (টন/হেক্টর)","parenthetical crop qualifiers","comments in col 5, which must wrap extensively"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [90, 87, 89, 63, 89] · table 419×2650px · row heights [83, 501, 385, 432, 362, 432, 455] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 21 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 59px
Design r1B: widths [90, 87, 89, 63, 111] · table 441×1859px · row heights [83, 339, 269, 315, 292, 269, 292] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 14 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 81px
Design r1C: widths [90, 88, 90, 63, 140] · table 472×1417px · row heights [83, 269, 199, 222, 199, 199, 246] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 11 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 112px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"Cols 1–4 sit at their true minimums, so no crop name, season word or unit is broken; only 59px of overflow, so almost everything is reachable with one small nudge.","problems":"Visually it collapses: the মন্তব্য column is a 2–3-words-per-line ribbon 21 lines deep, rows swell to 500px, and the table runs 2650px — roughly seven phone screens. Reading a comment means reading a vertical word list, and the eye can no longer associate the note with its crop row.","cause":"col 5 = 89px gives only 68px of text for a column whose one-line content is 1035px; the whole budget was spent holding cols 2–3 at their unbreakable-word minimums, but they are not what sets row height — col 5 is."},{"design":"r1B","good":"Recognises that col 5, not the timing pair, drives height and starts paying width to it; 1859px and 14-line cells is a real improvement, still with zero mid-word splits.","problems":"Still the wrong side of the readability threshold — 90px of text is under four short words per line, so comments remain unscannable and rows are 270–340px. 81px of overflow also buys very little: you scroll right and still get a cramped comment.","cause":"col 5 = 111px (90px text) against 1035px of content ≈ 12–14 lines; the 22px added over r1A is spread too thin to change the line count materially."},{"design":"r1C","good":"Best of the three: 1417px, comments down to 11 lines, rows 200–270px, headers all one line except the intentionally stacked ফলন (টন/হেক্টর), no splits. (1) 112px of overflow means that when the reader scrolls right to read the comment, col 1 and half of col 2 leave the screen — the crop name, the row anchor, is gone exactly when the note is being read. (2) The date ranges in cols 2–3 still break to 3–4 short lines, and the em dash lands at line end (“সপ্তাহ—” / “জানুয়ারির”), so the sowing→harvest window does not read as one phrase.","cause":"col 5 = 140px (119px text) is still only ~1/9 of the column's content width, so 11 lines remain; and cols 2–3 at 88/90px carry 263/239px one-line content, i.e. three-plus wraps each."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"comment-195","widths":[90,87,89,63,195],"change":"Keep cols 1–4 at the proven minimums (no splits, tight timing block) and move all discretionary width into the height driver: col 5 at 195px (174px text) brings comments to ~6 lines and rows to ~150px, cutting the table from 1417 to roughly 1000px. Accepts 165px of scroll, but that scroll now buys a readable note instead of a one-word-per-line ribbon."},{"name":"comment-250","widths":[90,87,89,63,250],"change":"Push the same logic further: 229px of comment text gives ~4–5 lines per row, so rows become near-uniform (~130px) and the whole table fits in about two screens. Overflow grows to 224px, so this is the 'read the notes as prose' extreme; choose it only if the comments are the payload rather than the garnish."},{"name":"timing-plus-185","widths":[90,115,110,63,185],"change":"Alternative spend: give cols 2–3 enough room (94/89px of text) to hold a date range in two lines with the em dash inside a line, so the sowing→harvest pair finally reads as one phrase — the table's primary scan. col 5 stays at a still-workable 185px (~6 lines). Costs 239px of overflow; the trade is legible season columns at the price of a longer horizontal swipe."}]}
